judgment_calls: Requirement 1's receipt-filtering wiring is scoped to the PROMOTE branch only (a new async gateProductionPromotionAsync re-checks a promote decision against listReceiptBackedByExperimentAsync-filtered cohorts under the SAME decideExperiment stopping rule). regress/inconclusive/collecting decisions continue to read the unfiltered ledger via listByExperimentAsync, matching the contract's global invariant text ('No experiment may establish outcome_status=verified unless both cohorts contain valid, finalized treatment receipts...') which names 'verified' specifically. This preserves ~20 pre-existing W6/C0/C2 tests (documented in issue-1450.json's own c4 criterion as deliberately deferred to C3) that assert regress/inconclusive reachability over unfiltered ledger fixtures with no receipts, while still making promote/verified require real treatment-v2 receipts end-to-end (proven by a new passing test).

Requirement 2's 'internally inconsistent verdict/evidence pair' exclusion is scoped narrowly to DIRECT, provable self-contradictions inside the objective-success-rate metric itself (a stored 'success' verdict paired with terminalStatus in {error, aborted}, producedArtifact===false, or errorCount>0) rather than a full recomputation-equality check against finalizeVerdict. A full-recomputation check would have excluded essentially every pre-existing test fixture in the repo (which routinely uses null/unknown evidence with an asserted verdict for fixture convenience), which is ambiguous/absent evidence, not a contradiction. finalizeVerdict's own existing write-time behavior (rule 3: absent artifact evidence never yields success) is preserved and covered by a dedicated regression test for requirement 3, rather than re-implemented as a second, read-time filter.

Requirement 6's guardrail breach check runs synchronously (no cross-process lock) inside reserveRunEnrollment, immediately before cohort assignment. A racing concurrent reservation could in principle still slip through once between the guardrail evaluation and the recordDecisionAsync write; recordDecisionAsync's own 'WHERE decision IS NULL' guard is the same level of atomicity this codebase already relies on for the exposure cap and idempotent reservation elsewhere. Full multi-process transactional guardrail enforcement is not attempted in this phase.

Guardrail rate thresholds (terminal-error-rate > 0.5, treatment-integrity-failure-rate > 0.3) and the response-rate imbalance ceiling (0.2) are fixed constants, not per-bundle configurable, matching the fixed/closed style of EXPERIMENT_ADAPTERS and the guardrail registry itself. Marked with ponytail comments naming the upgrade path (a declared bundle field) if a real proposal needs a different bound.
